If a rip current grabs you, do not swim back to shore.
A rip is a river of water running out to sea, and the strongest move as fast as an Olympic swimmer.
Fight it and you tire out. That is how people drown.
But a rip will not pull you under. And it is usually less than a hundred yards wide.
So turn sideways. Swim along the beach until the pull lets go.
Then swim back in at an angle.
Too tired to swim? Relax, face the shore, and wave for help.
See someone else caught in one? Do not swim out after them.
Throw them something that floats, and get a lifeguard.
And before you get in, look for the calm, dark gap between the breaking waves. That gap is the rip.
Better still, swim where the lifeguards are.
